title: Comparison map for a proper map fixing an open
statement:
Let $T_1,T_2,X$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $u:T_1\to T_2$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $j_i:X\hookrightarrow T_i$ be open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] with $u\circ j_1=j_2$. Fix a finite commutative ring $\Lambda$ and $K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Use the derived direct image $Ru_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], and inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

Put $V=T_1\times_{T_2}X$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $b:V\to T_1$ and $p:V\to X$. Define $s:X\to V$ by the pair $(j_1,\operatorname{id}_X)$, so $b\circ s=j_1$ and $p\circ s=\operatorname{id}_X$. The base-change identification of [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] identifies $V$ with the open subscheme $u^{-1}(j_2(X))$ of $T_1$. Under this identification, $s$ is the inclusion of the open subscheme $j_1(X)$ into $u^{-1}(j_2(X))$: the inclusion of images follows from $u\circ j_1=j_2$, and the structure sheaf maps are the restrictions of those of $j_1$. Thus $s$ is an open immersion. The morphism $p$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], hence separated; [lem-weil-pbc-open-section-clopen] makes $s(X)$ open and closed in $V$.

Specify the three isomorphisms used in the construction as follows. Let
$$
 r_{u,K}:j_2^{-1}Ru_*j_{1!}K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*b^{-1}j_{1!}K
$$
be the open-restriction isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-open-restriction], applied to $u,j_2,j_{1!}K$. The square with top map $\operatorname{id}_X:X\to X$, left map $s:X\to V$, right map $j_1:X\to T_1$, and bottom map $b:V\to T_1$ is an open-immersion square [def-cbc-open-immersion-square]. Indeed an open immersion is a monomorphism: after identifying its source with an open subscheme, a morphism into it is uniquely determined by its composite with the inclusion, including the restricted structure sheaf maps. For every scheme $Z$, a pair $t:Z\to X$, $v:Z\to V$ with $j_1t=bv$ satisfies $b s t=j_1t=bv$, hence $v=st$. Thus the fibre-product universal property gives $X\times_{T_1}V\cong X$, with inverse to its first projection given by $(\operatorname{id}_X,s)$. Let
$$
 e_{u,K}:b^{-1}j_{1!}K\xrightarrow{\sim}s_!K
$$
be the canonical base-change isomorphism of [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change] for this square, using the identity inverse-image identification on $X$. Let
$$
 c_{p,s,K}:Rp_*s_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}K
$$
be the component-restriction isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-clopen-section-direct-image]. Define the specified isomorphism by the composite
$$
 \theta_{u,K}=c_{p,s,K}\circ Rp_*(e_{u,K})\circ r_{u,K}:
 j_2^{-1}Ru_*j_{1!}K\xrightarrow{\sim}K.
$$

Use the adjunction $j_{2!}\dashv j_2^{-1}$ on $D^+$ induced by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. Here both sheaf functors are exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] and [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; apply them termwise to complexes and homotopy classes as in [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. Their units and counits descend through the localization by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], and the triangle identities descend with them. These induced exact functors preserve $D^+$ by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below]. Write $\varepsilon_{j_2}:j_{2!}j_2^{-1}\to\operatorname{id}$ for the descended counit. Define the comparison map to be the adjoint of $\theta_{u,K}^{-1}$, explicitly
$$
 \alpha_{u,K}:=
 \varepsilon_{j_2,Ru_*j_{1!}K}\circ j_{2!}(\theta_{u,K}^{-1}):
 j_{2!}K\longrightarrow Ru_*j_{1!}K.
$$
All composites and inverse isomorphisms are taken in the indicated bounded below derived categories.

proof.text: For s = pullback.lift j₁ (id X), the projection identities are s ≫ b = j₁ and s ≫ p = id X. Base change of the open immersion j₂ makes b an open immersion. Rewrite s ≫ b as j₁, then apply Mathlib IsOpenImmersion.of_comp to obtain IsOpenImmersion s.

The projection p is proper by base change of f, hence separated. Rewrite s ≫ p as the identity to obtain a closed immersion. Apply IsClosedImmersion.of_comp to s and p. The closed embedding underlying this closed immersion has closed range. This proves only the closed-image clause needed here; the complementary coproduct assertion of open_section_clopen is unnecessary.
The square (id X, s, j₁, b) commutes by s ≫ b = j₁. The identity is an isomorphism and the open immersion b is a monomorphism, so Mathlib IsPullback.of_horiz_isIso_mono proves it Cartesian.

Keep the specified isomorphism θ: compose the canonical derived open-restriction exchange r, the image under Rp_* of extension-zero base change e followed by identity inverse-image identification, and the uniquely characterized component-restriction isomorphism c for the now-proved clopen section.

Keep the comparison α as extension by zero applied to θ inverse followed by the counit of the existing derived extension-zero/restriction adjunction. No termwise-adjunction construction or exactness proof is repeated in this module.
